annotations.title: Let his hart be changed.
annotations.text: In what maner king Nabuchodonosor was changed is hard to explicate. ◦ But omitting other opinions, the most probable and common is, that he was not depriued of his reasonable soule, nor the forme and partes of his bodie substantially changed from the nature of a man: but he was distracted losing the vse of reason, and in his owne melancholie imagination and phantasie, thought that he was a beast. And therfore easily refused the conuersation of men, and consorted himself with beasts; went naked; his hayre growing very much, and couering al his bodie; his nayles likewise extreme long; he went on his handes together with his feete, like fourfooted beastes; did eate grasse as an oxe, putting his mouth to the ground, to shere and swalowe it, the space of seuen yeares. Then God restoring to him the vse of reason, and inspiring him with grace, he lifted vp his eyes to heauen (v.31.) and in perfect sense blessed God, the Highest, and praysed him; was againe receiued, yea sought for by his nobles and magistrates: so was restored to his kingdom, and had more magnificence then before.

notes.text: Nabuchodonosor was not chaged in substance; but became madde, and liued seuen yeares like a beast.

annotations.title: Now therfore I Nabuchodonosor praise, magnifie, and glorifie God.
annotations.text: Albeit holie Scripture doth not reporte, when and how king Nabuchodonosor died, [1] yet by this last thing written of him, it is very like he liued not long after his great chastisment: for if he had, it is probable that Daniel would haue written more of him, & that he being so fully conuerted to God, would haue deliuered Ioachin king of Iuda, out of prison (which his next successor Euilmerodach did. 4. Reg. 25. v. 27.) and al the Iewes from captiuitie, if God had longer spared him life, he being now wel affected towards them. [2] And that he died in state of saluation, may with great reason be supposed, seing his repentance and conuersion to God is so fully expressed in holie Scripture, and no mention that he fel againe. Which is also the iudgement of most lerned writers, Namely of Iosephus. li. 10. Antiq. Dorotheus in Synopsi. S. Epiphanius, in vita Danielis. S. Ierom. epist. 7. ad Letam. S. Augustin epist. 122. ad Victoriam, & li. de predest & gratia c. 15. Where he compareth Pharao with Nabuchodonosor, and their diuers endes, by Gods grace mouing the one to penance for his iniquitie, the other wilfully fighting against Gods merciful veritie. as we haue noted. Exo. 7. pag. 174.

notes.text: It is probable that he died shortly after his restauration.
And most like that he is eternally saued.
